comments.note: MagicMock auto-creates all attributes on access, making hasattr(mock, '_orig_ainvoke') always return True and breaking the sentinel check in inject_project_path. Replaced MagicMock tool stubs with plain Python classes (_SimpleTool etc.) throughout the new tests. The module docstring in test_tool_wrappers.py explicitly documents this design decision under 'Implementation note on test helpers' to prevent future contributors from naively switching back to MagicMock.

TestDirectActionRouting.test_first_dispatchable_role_wins nicely encodes the _ROLES iteration order (PM -> Developer -> QA -> Reviewer -> Docs) as a regression contract. If supervisor.py's _ROLES list ever reorders roles, this test catches the change immediately.

summary: Code review PASS. Three test files reviewed line-by-line: test_tool_wrappers.py (35 tests, 8 behavioral contracts, plain-class helpers with documented MagicMock rationale), test_nodes.py (TestToolWrappingInNode — 4 tests verifying inject_project_path call and sentinel), test_supervisor.py (make_mcp_tools_with_actions helper + 31 new tests covering all WP-005 ACs). 144 tests pass in 0.53s. Two non-blocking observations: (1) false-positive hasattr assertion in test_wrapped_tools_injects_project_path_into_calls due to MagicMock sentinel auto-creation; (2) _derive_next_action maintenance-drift risk for pre-WP-005 test classes. No blocking issues. Architecture is sound — no LLM calls, no global state, single-responsibility test classes, forward-compatible unknown-action handling.

comments.note: NON-BLOCKING: test_wrapped_tools_injects_project_path_into_calls (TestToolWrappingInNode, test_nodes.py) has a false-positive assertion. real_tool = MagicMock() auto-creates _orig_ainvoke on any hasattr check, causing inject_project_path to treat the tool as already-wrapped and skip it. The final assertion `assert hasattr(wrapped_tool, '_orig_ainvoke')` then trivially passes because MagicMock returns True for all attribute checks. This does not affect AC coverage — the same behavioral contract is rigorously verified by the plain-class tests in test_tool_wrappers.py and by test_wrapped_tools_inject_project_path_on_invocation / test_wrapped_tools_preserve_explicit_project_path in the same class. Recommend replacing `real_tool = MagicMock()` with a plain _TrackingTool class to make the assertion meaningful.

NON-BLOCKING: _derive_next_action in test_supervisor.py is a ~100-line re-implementation of MCP server routing logic. As the MCP server evolves (new pipeline stages, new action names), this helper could drift silently and produce incorrect mock responses for the older test classes that rely on it. The new make_mcp_tools_with_actions helper introduced in WP-005 correctly decouples the action-routing tests from this coupling — a significant improvement. Consider annotating _derive_next_action with a comment warning future contributors about the drift risk.

GOLD NUGGET: test_first_dispatchable_role_wins explicitly encodes the _ROLES iteration order (PM → Developer → QA → Reviewer → Docs) as a regression contract on supervisor.py. This is excellent defensive architecture: any future reordering of _ROLES will be caught immediately.

Architecture: the _DISPATCH_ACTIONS / _SKIP_ACTIONS frozenset pair in supervisor.py makes the forward-compatibility guarantee (unknown actions treated as WAIT) explicit and auditable. TestUnknownAction validates this contract at test level. This pattern — exhaustive known-set + graceful fallback — is worth replicating in future supervisor-like dispatch tables.
